questions.stem: Simplify the expression: ((p AND q) OR (r AND s))

choices.B: p OR q OR r OR s
choices.C: p AND q AND r AND s

questions.solution: The expression simplifies to (p OR r) AND (q OR s), using the distributive property of logical operators. Options B, C, and D are incorrect because they either represent a different relationship or do not follow the correct operator precedence.
questions.explanation: When simplifying expressions with conjunctions (AND) and disjunctions (OR), we can use the distributive property to group terms.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to forget the distributive property, leading to an incorrect simplification.

questions.stem: Simplify the expression: p AND True
questions.solution: The expression simplifies to True, as any value ANDed with True results in True. Options A, B, and D are incorrect because they represent a different relationship.
questions.explanation: In logical expressions, the identity laws state that any value ANDed with True or ORed with False results in the other value.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to forget the identity laws, leading to an incorrect simplification.

questions.stem: Simplify the expression: NOT(p) OR q
questions.solution: The expression simplifies to NOT(p) AND q, which is equivalent to the original expression due to the material implication rule. Options A, C, and D are incorrect because they represent a different relationship.
questions.explanation: In logical expressions, the material implication (p implies q) can be represented as NOT(p) OR q, and vice versa.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to confuse the material implication with other logical relationships, leading to an incorrect simplification.

questions.stem: Simplify the expression: (p XOR q) AND NOT(p)
questions.solution: The expression simplifies to q, as p XOR q AND NOT(p) means either p is false and q is true (exclusive OR), and since we know NOT(p) is true, q must be true. Options B, C, and D are incorrect because they represent a different relationship.
questions.explanation: When simplifying expressions involving exclusive OR (XOR), we consider the truth table for XOR to determine the simplified form.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to misinterpret the exclusive OR, leading to an incorrect simplification.

questions.stem: Simplify the expression: (p implies q) AND (q implies p)
questions.solution: The expression simplifies to p AND q, as both implications imply a biconditional relationship (p if and only if q). Options A, C, and D are incorrect because they represent different relationships.
questions.explanation: When combining two implications in opposite directions, the result is a biconditional statement (p AND q) or (q AND p), depending on the order of the variables.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to overlook the relationship between converse implications and biconditionals, leading to an incorrect simplification.
